newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan coffee body opposes sale of key plant.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan coffee body opposes sale of key plant.

text.p: A senior official of the state-run Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) urged the government to proceed with caution in its plans to sell 51 percent of the coffee marketing board, after only one firm bid for it.
President Yoweri Museveni, responding to UCDA concerns, also urged caution in the sale and detailed a cabinet minister to study the matter further before a final decision.
UCDA and a number of other Ugandan industry players are particularly concerned over the sale of the giant Bugoloobi processing plant outside Kampala.
This is being offered for sale along with eight coffee processing plants, two residential houses in the capital and some storage facilities upcountry.
Together these operations make up 51 percent in the government-owned Coffee Marketing Board Ltd (CMBL), according to bid documents sent to Reuters on Tuesday.

The documents show the government as retaining 49 percent of its shareholding in the marketing board. But it will also sell such non-core assets as residential houses abroad, a fleet of trucks and other vehicles and a huge coffee storage facility at the Kenyan port of Mombasa.
Museveni told reporters on Monday that coffee was a crucial Ugandan export and any problems seen by UCDA needed attention.

Swiss company Sucafina, the only bidder, offered to pay $3.3 million for 51 percent of the board, including the Bugoloobi plant, which has an annual processing capacity of up to four million 60-kg bags of coffee.
The plant is valued at $8.8 million, according to bid documents. The CMBL is valued at a total of $36 million.
"In my view, it is not wise to sell off CMBL," the official told Reuters.
"The government must maintain a buyer of last resort. Even in Ivory Coast, when they liberalised, they retained the monopoly, which had 15 percent of the market share," he added.
UCDA is Uganda's top coffee policy monitoring agency. The official said his views were commonly held in UCDA ranks.
Under the purchase agreements, the new buyers would have management rights and the government would have no special minority rights despite its 49 percent shareholding.
"This is taking a big gamble. The industry should not be left entirely to the whims of the market," the UCDA official said, referring to Sucafina solely managing the Bugoloobi plant.
UCDA officials have said an alternative to the sale would be joint ownership of the Bugoloobi plant or better still, for the government to withdraw it from the sale offer.
Coffee accounts for 70 percent of Uganda's hard-currency revenues. Privatisation officials said they were still evaluating the bid by Sucafina.
Uganda is Africa's largest coffee producer, ahead of Ivory Coast and Ethiopia.
